item.title: Takeaways from the Trump-Xi state visit: Pageantry and pandas
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping praised the level of "perfection" on display during his state visit to the White House, and President Donald Trump said Friday the two world leaders had a "very productive" time in Washington. Trump, speaking to reporters as he and first lady Melania Trump hosted Xi and first lady of China Madame Peng Liyuan for tea at the White House, said, "We've had a tremendous visit from two spectacular people," and, "we've made great strides, very positive for both countries." "I want to thank the honorable president and the first lady for everything they've done for myself and my wife during this visit. Everything is down to the highest order of perfection," Xi responded through a translator. "And there is thought in every little detail. And it's greatly appreciated. item.title: White House TV pool is back in operation after a dayslong ban of news outlets from grounds
item.description:
Reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico were readmitted to the White House for the first time since Friday, hours after a judge ordered the Trump administration to immediately reinstate their credentials. Why it matters: The reinstatement should mark the end of a broader press boycott that left the American public without key visual coverage of President Trump over the past few days. State of play: As of 1pm ET, it was unclear whether television pool cameras would be in place to cover President Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The major networks in the rotating television pool were still waiting on confirmation from the White House that CNN would be allowed to manage those duties. item.title: Hurricane Nolo threatening Hawaii with heavy rain as Polo churns near Mexico
item.description:
Area’s second-most intense hurricane on record being fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system in a Pacific hurricane season that has been notably active in recent months. On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for the system to maintain its considerable strength. Polo is expected to turn towards the west-north-west, before taking a more north-westerly trajectory on Saturday. It has maximum sustained winds of around 150mph, with even stronger gusts occurring within the most intense parts of the hurricane. item.title: Manchester City reportedly found guilty of almost 115 financial charges
item.description:
The Premier League has reportedly given Manchester City a major red card. City has been found guilty of more than 100 financial charges that were brought by the league over an eight-year period, according to a report from The Athletic. The punishment has not been decided, and City is expected to appeal potential sanctions, according to the report. "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023," City told The Athletic in a statement. item.title: Xi wraps up US visit with trip to National Archives
item.description:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping departed Washington this afternoon after a three-day trip that led to no significant breakthroughs on the two country’s disagreements, including on AI, Taiwan and Iran. Xi broached Taiwan to Trump, per a readout from Beijing, and Trump asked Xi to stop supporting Iran , US Ambassador to Beijing David Perdue said . Officials also discussed extending their trade truce until January and staying in touch about AI, Treasury Department Scott Bessent said earlier this week. But there were no major announcements with the countries still at odds on most fronts, including its growing nuclear arsenal. That could change later this year, when Xi said he would see Trump at the APEC summit in China and the G20 summit in the US. Xi also invited Trump back to China in the spring. item.title: Macron says ‘military resources’ to be sent to Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis, pushing oil prices up on fears the Middle East conflict could expand and intensify. Though Riyadh recently signed a mutual defense agreement with Pakistan and Türkiye, neither has been willing to deploy troops to help the kingdom, forcing Saudi Arabia to turn to European countries for assistance. The Trump administration has also failed to come to Saudi Arabia’s aid despite their long-term defense relations, a decision that risks further fraying ties between the erstwhile allies. Saudi Arabia’s de facto ruler “ will not forget this ,” a former senior US defense official told the Financial Times. — Jeronimo Gonzalez
